label: Chicago

county_election_office.name: Chicago Board of Election Commissioners (City of Chicago voters), 69 W. Washington St., 6th floor. Suburban Cook voters use the Cook County Clerk instead.

zip_caveats: ZIP codes don't decide your ballot; your address does. Look up your exact ballot with the Chicago Board of Elections ('Your Voter Information' at chicagoelections.gov) or VOTE411 before you print a cheat sheet. Every Chicago voter sees: the statewide races; Cook County Board President, Clerk, Sheriff, Treasurer and Assessor; both MWRD races; the Appellate Court seat; the five countywide Circuit Court vacancies; all 59 judicial retention questions; the school board president race; the Cook County millionaire question; the three citywide questions; and the two CPS questions. Everything else depends on where you live: congressional district, Illinois Senate and House district, Cook County Board district, Board of Review district (only Districts 1 and 2 vote this year), judicial subcircuit, school board subdistrict, and any ward or precinct question. Each of these lines splits ZIP codes. Logan Square (60647): Wikipedia's district description puts Logan Square in the 3rd Congressional District (Delia Ramirez). Neighboring West Town is split between the 3rd and 7th, so the eastern edge of 60647 may vote in the 7th; confirm with the lookup. We could not confirm which Illinois House and Senate districts, County Board district, Board of Review district, judicial subcircuit or school board subdistrict cover 60647; each splits the ZIP. 60647 is also split among several wards. Ward and precinct questions appear only in the ward or precinct named. This year that includes a 26th Ward question on limiting new short-term rentals, which matters only if your address is in the 26th Ward. The Mid-Northside mental health tax questions appear only inside that territory, whose boundaries we could not confirm. Edges: border ZIPs such as 60707 and 60827 include suburban addresses that vote with the Cook County Clerk (cookcountyclerkil.gov), not the Chicago board. Some districts listed here are mostly suburban and reach only small parts of the city (IL-6, IL-8, House District 55).

heads_up.text: Questions labeled advisory are nonbinding. Local-option questions about alcohol sales are binding.
